translations.Keep the cup, milk amount and starting p: Keep the cup, milk amount and starting position consistent. Lower the pitcher at the same fill level each time. Compare the shape and symmetry before changing one part of your pour.
translations.Repeat the same preparation for two shot: Repeat the same preparation for two shots.
translations.Use the same dose, distribution routine: Use the same dose, distribution routine and level tamp. Keep the recipe unchanged. Compare flow and taste, then choose one preparation step to practise next time.
Smell your espresso and name one aroma.
Before tasting, pause to smell the cup. Write down one familiar food or aroma it reminds you of. Taste, then see whether your first impression changes as the drink cools.
translations.Pour a centred white circle with a clean: Pour a centred white circle with a clean edge.
translations.First mix milk into the espresso from a: First mix milk into the espresso from a little higher up. Bring the spout close to the surface and pour steadily in the centre. Practise a round base before adding a pull-through.
translations.Repeat a favourite shot without adjustme: Repeat a favourite shot without adjustments.
translations.Keep beans, dose, grind and target yield: Keep beans, dose, grind and target yield the same. Taste both shots before checking the numbers. Note whether the sensory result agrees with the apparent consistency.
translations.Describe your cup without saying good or: Describe your cup without saying good or bad.
translations.Choose one word for aroma, one for mouth: Choose one word for aroma, one for mouthfeel and one for the finish. A description such as cocoa, syrupy and lingering is easier to compare with your next shot than a score alone.
translations.Does the acidity remind you of lemon or: Does the acidity remind you of lemon or orange?
translations.Smell, take a small sip and let the cup: Smell, take a small sip and let the cup cool before tasting again. Look for a familiar citrus impression rather than trying to force a particular note. None is a useful answer too.
translations.Think cocoa powder, dark chocolate or mi: Think cocoa powder, dark chocolate or milk chocolate.
translations.Compare aroma, sweetness and bitterness: Compare aroma, sweetness and bitterness separately. Decide which chocolate reference feels closest, if any. A flavour association does not mean the coffee contains that ingredient.
translations.Fresh fruit, dried fruit, or no fruit at: Fresh fruit, dried fruit, or no fruit at all?
translations.Start with a broad family before naming: Start with a broad family before naming a specific fruit. Compare the aroma with the aftertaste. Try again as the espresso cools and notice whether your description becomes more specific.
translations.Is the cup light, silky, syrupy or dryin: Is the cup light, silky, syrupy or drying?
translations.Focus on how the coffee feels rather tha: Focus on how the coffee feels rather than its flavour. Notice its weight on your tongue and the feeling left after swallowing. Keep body and a drying finish as separate observations.
translations.Look for a honey, caramel or ripe-fruit: Look for a honey, caramel or ripe-fruit impression.
translations.Taste the espresso without additions fir: Taste the espresso without additions first. Notice whether its aroma suggests sweetness even when the drink is bitter. Record your own association; there is no required tasting note.
Wait a few moments before the next sip. Describe the lingering flavour and whether it feels pleasant, clean or drying. Compare that finish with your impression at the start of the sip.
translations.Compare two yields with the same dose an: Compare two yields with the same dose and grind.
translations.For example, try 18g in with 32g out, th: For example, try 18g in with 32g out, then 40g out. Keep other settings fixed and stir both cups. Compare strength, sweetness and finish. These are tasting experiments, not universal targets.
translations.Taste the same espresso at three tempera: Taste the same espresso at three temperatures.
translations.Take small sips as the cup naturally coo: Take small sips as the cup naturally cools. Note changes in aroma, sweetness, acidity and texture. Keep the recipe fixed: the only thing you are comparing is the temperature in the cup.
translations.Compare espresso with a little added wat: Compare espresso with a little added water.
translations.Stir a shot and divide it between two cu: Stir a shot and divide it between two cups. Add a measured amount of warm water to one. Compare flavour clarity and body. Dilution changes strength after brewing without changing extraction.
translations.Compare two recipes without seeing their: Compare two recipes without seeing their labels.
translations.Ask someone to label two cups underneath: Ask someone to label two cups underneath and mix up their positions. Taste before revealing which recipe is which. Write down your preference and a reason before looking at shot statistics.
translations.Compare the same espresso with two milk: Compare the same espresso with two milk amounts.
translations.Split a stirred shot evenly between two: Split a stirred shot evenly between two cups. Add different measured amounts of the same prepared milk. Compare coffee intensity, sweetness and texture, then note your preferred balance.
translations.Change only the grind for your next comp: Change only the grind for your next comparison.
Keep beans, dose and target yield fixed. Make a small grinder adjustment and follow its normal retention routine. Compare taste and flow; a longer shot time alone does not establish a better result.
translations.Keep dose and grind fixed. A longer yiel: Keep dose and grind fixed. A longer yield may soften sharpness but also reduces strength. If flow is uneven, improve puck preparation first. Some acidity is part of the coffee; compare by taste.
translations.Hold dose and grind steady and stop a li: Hold dose and grind steady and stop a little earlier. Compare the finish. Roast character can also contribute bitterness, so use the result to decide whether this direction helps.
translations.Explore a shorter ratio for more strengt: Explore a shorter ratio for more strength.
translations.At the same dose, reduce the yield sligh: At the same dose, reduce the yield slightly and compare body. This also changes extraction. If the cup becomes sharp or sour, revisit grind and evenness instead of shortening it further.
Check evenness before chasing shot time.
translations.A drying finish can accompany uneven ext: A drying finish can accompany uneven extraction. Repeat with careful distribution and a level tamp. Compare taste before trying a small grind or yield adjustment.
Check puck preparation and uneven flow.
translations.Both sensations can occur together. Keep: Both sensations can occur together. Keep the recipe steady and improve distribution first. If flow is erratic or choking, test a slightly coarser grind and compare the next cup.
Keep this recipe as your reference.
translations.Repeat the same dose, grind and yield be: Repeat the same dose, grind and yield before experimenting further. Note what you enjoy about the cup. A satisfying result is a better reference than chasing a particular shot time.
translations.Pour over ice and tonic slowly: Pour over ice and tonic slowly

translations.A steady central pour makes a clean whit: A steady central pour makes a clean white circle.
translations.Espresso describes a brewing method, not: Espresso describes a brewing method, not a particular bean or roast level.
translations.A finer grind usually slows a shot becau: A finer grind usually slows a shot because it creates more resistance to water flow.
translations.Crema is a foam of coffee oils, suspende: Crema is a foam of coffee oils, suspended solids and carbon dioxide released under pressure.
translations.A 1:2 brew ratio means the beverage weig: A 1:2 brew ratio means the beverage weighs twice as much as the dry coffee dose.
translations.Pre-infusion gently wets the puck before: Pre-infusion gently wets the puck before full pressure and can help reduce uneven flow.
translations.Freshly roasted coffee releases carbon d: Freshly roasted coffee releases carbon dioxide, which changes how a shot extracts over time.
translations.Water chemistry can strongly influence b: Water chemistry can strongly influence both extraction and the flavours perceived in the cup.
translations.Temperature, pressure and flow describe: Temperature, pressure and flow describe different parts of a shot; no single metric tells the whole story.
translations.A bottomless portafilter makes uneven fl: A bottomless portafilter makes uneven flow easier to see, but it does not fix puck preparation.
translations.The word espresso comes from Italian and: The word espresso comes from Italian and is associated with coffee prepared expressly to order.
